collection.description: An elder who used to swim every day watches the children in the shallows: wade in, or just dip their feet.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) used to swim every day. Out past the reef and back, before breakfast. Then (his/her) knees started to complain, and the water seemed colder, and somehow (he/she) stopped. That was years ago. Today, watching the children splash in the shallows, (name1) finds (him/her)self taking off (his/her) sandals.

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: The water is cold. Then it's not. (name1) lies back and floats, and the sea holds (him/her) up exactly the way it used to. (He/She) doesn't go out to the reef. (He/She) doesn't need to. (He/She) just floats there, looking at the sky, while the children swim round (him/her) like little fish. When (he/she) comes out, (his/her) knees ache. (He/She) decides it was worth it.

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: (name1) sits on a rock and lowers (his/her) feet into the water. It's cold, and lovely, and familiar. That's enough for today, (he/she) decides. The children splash (him/her), and (he/she) splashes them back, and nobody notices that (he/she) is smiling at something that has nothing to do with them.
